caption:
One son buried, another on life support. A father's world collapses as measles, dengue, and pneumonia strike his children.

A 10-year-old boy, Nur Mohammad Arafat, died on Friday after battling measles, dengue, and pneumonia. He was a third-grade student at Hillview Public School in Chattogram.

topic: World Bank commits $300mn to boost primary education
headline_marked: World Bank [[commits $300 million to boost primary education]] in Bangladesh
headline: World Bank commits $300 million to boost primary education in Bangladesh
summary: The loan aims to improve reading, writing, and math skills for 26 million children from pre-primary to Class 5.
details: The World Bank has approved a $300 million loan to enhance the quality of primary education in Bangladesh. The funding will target 26 million children from pre-primary to Class 5, focusing on foundational literacy and numeracy.
The loan, provided by the International Development Association (IDA), is equivalent to approximately Tk 37.35 billion. It features a 25-year repayment period, including a five-year grace period.

While Bangladesh has achieved near-universal access to primary schooling, quality remains a significant challenge. According to the World Bank, nearly half of 10-year-olds struggle to understand simple, age-appropriate text.

The program will introduce a special package of teaching materials, structured lesson plans, and comprehensive teacher training. Additionally, head teachers at 90% of government primary schools will receive leadership and management training.

Lagging students will receive extra lessons, with priority given to the worst-hit districts. The initiative also aims to improve the quality of pre-primary education and ensure data-driven decision-making.
The World Bank expects this program to create 843,000 new, comparatively well-paid jobs in government primary schools, further strengthening the education system.
